chunks: Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both)
about the orchard whose produce is not sold, and even if sold, its produce amounts to wealth. Is zakat obligatory in it? He said, 'No, if it is consumed [as food].'
ai.seo_question: Is zakat obligatory on an orchard whose produce is consumed rather than sold?
ai.summary: This narration from the Al al-Bayt tradition highlights the Shia juristic distinction between agricultural produce intended for subsistence versus commercial trade, a key factor in determining zakat liability. It reflects the broader principle that zakat is primarily a tax on surplus and wealth accumulation, thereby exempting personal consumption from this obligation.
